events.title: Ansible first released
events.summary: Michael DeHaan open-sourced Ansible on February 20, 2012 — an agentless configuration management and automation tool using YAML playbooks.
events.about: Ansible SSHs into servers (or talks WinRM on Windows) and applies idempotent tasks — install packages, copy configs, restart services. No agent daemon required. Example: a playbook that installs nginx, templates `/etc/nginx/nginx.conf`, and ensures the service is running on ten hosts in parallel.

narrative.whyChosen: Ansible made infrastructure automation approachable with plain YAML and SSH.
narrative.whyImportant: It competed with Puppet and Chef and became Red Hat's default ops automation stack.
narrative.problemSolved: Complex agent-based config management was heavy; teams wanted simple, readable automation.

events.title: Raspberry Pi Model B released
events.summary: The Raspberry Pi Foundation opened Model B orders on February 29, 2012 — a $35 credit-card-sized Linux computer; first production units shipped in mid-April 2012.
events.about: Raspberry Pi runs Debian on ARM with GPIO pins for robotics, home automation, and retro gaming. Schools taught Python on Pis; makers built NAS boxes and media centers. It brought full Linux userspace to the same audience Arduino served at the microcontroller layer — and sold tens of millions of units.

narrative.whyChosen: The Model B made a complete Linux computer affordable for education and hobbyists.
narrative.whyImportant: It revived computer literacy in schools and powered countless IoT and maker projects.
narrative.problemSolved: Students and hobbyists could not experiment with real computers at microcontroller price points.
